headline: Jean Claude Saclag Takes Asian Games MMA Silver After Final Loss to Rajabov
seoTitle: Jean Claude Saclag Wins 2026 Asian Games MMA Silver | FMB News
seoDescription: Jean Claude Saclag won the Philippines' first silver medal of the 2026 Asian Games after a 0-3 loss to Tajikistan's Otabek Rajabov in the men's traditional -65kg MMA final.
deck: Saclag's gold-medal bid ended in a 0-3 decision against Tajikistan's Otabek Rajabov, converting the Filipino fighter's previously guaranteed medal into the Philippines' first silver of the 2026 Asian Games.
author: FMB News Sports Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Jean Claude Saclag won silver in the men's traditional -65kg mixed martial arts event at the 2026 Asian Games after losing 0-3 to Tajikistan's Otabek Rajabov in Tuesday's gold-medal match at Nagoya City Inae Sports Center.
The result gives the Philippines its first silver medal of the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Saclag had entered the final after a 3-0 semifinal victory over Japan's Daisuke Murayama.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Philippine News Agency, GMA News, ABS-CBN News and INQUIRER.net independently report Saclag's 0-3 final loss and silver-medal finish. The official Aichi-Nagoya venue schedule places the MMA final session at Nagoya City Inae Sports Center on September 22.
Saclag did not win the gold medal. Rajabov won the final; Saclag's completed result is silver.

sections.heading: Continuation
paragraphs: This is an independently newsworthy continuation of FMB News' earlier coverage of Saclag's Asian Games MMA run. Earliest relevant FMB News report: /news/saclag-alvarez-assured-asian-games-mma-medals-september-21-2026. The immediately preceding continuation, /news/saclag-asian-games-mma-final-alvarez-bronze-september-22-2026, reported his semifinal victory and guaranteed minimum silver before the final was contested.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Saclag's silver is the Philippines' highest-value medal of the Games so far and closes a medal run that began with his quarterfinal victory. MMA is making its Asian Games medal debut in Aichi-Nagoya, giving the result additional historical significance for Philippine combat sports.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Team Philippines continues its medal campaign across karate, gymnastics, boxing and other events. Saclag's completed MMA result no longer depends on a later bout or review in the sources checked for this report.

verificationNotes: The official Aichi-Nagoya venue schedule confirms the September 22 MMA final session at Nagoya City Inae Sports Center.
PNA, GMA News, ABS-CBN News and INQUIRER.net independently report Saclag's 0-3 loss to Otabek Rajabov and completed silver-medal result.
The story is explicitly a continuation of FMB News' September 21 quarterfinal report and September 22 semifinal report, not a duplicate of either.
The article does not describe Saclag as Asian Games champion; the confirmed completed result is silver.
The contextual venue photograph is KKPCW's own work on Wikimedia Commons under CC BY-SA 4.0 and is accurately labeled as a 2020 file photograph.
